source.title: Teacher-Student Curriculum Learning
source.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems

confidence_rationale: The closest mechanistic analogue in this pull to what ARC-019 actually commits to: advancement driven by a measured competence signal rather than a fixed schedule. TSCL selects sub-tasks by the slope of the student's learning curve and additionally revisits tasks whose performance is degrading, and matches or surpasses hand-crafted curricula on decimal addition and Minecraft navigation, solving tasks that were otherwise unsolvable. Mapping fidelity is the highest here because the gate is a competence criterion in a sequential RL setting. Confidence is capped by the same non-degeneracy problem ARC-019 itself flags: where the flat baseline cannot solve the task at all, the comparison shows the curriculum is *necessary for traversal*, not that it produces better outcomes at matched budget.
failure_signatures: TSCL's advantage is largest exactly where the ungated baseline fails outright, which is the V3-EXQ-591 degenerate-comparison shape in mirror image -- a REE result of this form would confirm the substrate needs a curriculum to traverse the task, not that ARC-019's outcome-quality claim holds.

The teacher gates on learning-progress slope, not on the fixed 7-criterion developmental gate REE uses; if progress-gating is what does the work, REE's fixed DEV-NEED-008 criteria could be the wrong gate and a staged-arm null would then be evidence against the *criteria*, not against staged development.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A Teacher that automatically chooses sub-tasks on which the Student is making the fastest learning progress (and revisits tasks where performance is worsening) matches or surpasses carefully hand-crafted curricula, and solves tasks unsolvable by uniform sampling.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-019's phase-advance gate is a coarser instance of the same device: hold the agent on a phase until a competence signal says move on. TSCL supports the general form of the commitment -- criterion-driven progression through sub-tasks is architecturally productive in sequential learners -- and additionally suggests REE's fixed criteria are a special case of a family in which adaptive, progress-derived gates are at least as good.
mapping.mapping_caveat: TSCL's tasks are an explicitly enumerated set with a designer-supplied decomposition and a dense per-task score; REE's phases are developmental stages in a single continuous embodied environment with a 7-criterion gate that is itself under test. The paper also does not report a matched-total-budget flat control that succeeds -- so it evidences 'curriculum enables traversal', which ARC-019 treats as a *precondition* to be verified, not as the finding.
mapping.source_context: Deep RL and LSTM supervised sequence tasks: decimal addition, Minecraft navigation; automatic curriculum via learning-progress teacher.

confidence_components.notes: Peer-reviewed journal version of a well-cited workshop line of work; lowest transfer risk in this pull because the setting is sequential RL with an explicit competence gate. Aggregate held to 0.63 by the degenerate-baseline issue, which is the single most important caveat for REE's use of this result.
